Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/bnxt_re: Avoid freeing MR resources if dereg fails

The driver returns an error code for MR dereg, but frees the MR structure.
When the MR dereg is retried due to previous error, the system crashes as
the structure is already freed.

Do not free the MR structures, when driver returns error to the stack.

Fixes: 872f3578241d ("RDMA/bnxt_re: Add support for MRs with Huge pages")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1574671174-5064-2-git-send-email-selvin.xavier@broadcom.com
Signed-off-by: Selvin Xavier <selvin.xavier@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
index 9b6ca15a183c..ad5112a2325f 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
@@ -3305,8 +3305,10 @@ int bnxt_re_dereg_mr(struct ib_mr *ib_mr, struct ib_udata *udata)
 	int rc;
 
 	rc = bnxt_qplib_free_mrw(&rdev->qplib_res, &mr->qplib_mr);
-	if (rc)
+	if (rc) {
 		dev_err(rdev_to_dev(rdev), "Dereg MR failed: %#x\n", rc);
+		return rc;
+	}
 
 	if (mr->pages) {
 		rc = bnxt_qplib_free_fast_reg_page_list(&rdev->qplib_res,

2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c`**
   - **Line Changes:**
     - The code block handling the deregistration of memory regions (MR) was modified. 
     - An error check was added after the call to `bnxt_qplib_free_mrw()`. If the return code (`rc`) indicates an error, a log message is generated using `dev_err()`, and the function returns the error code without proceeding to free the MR structure.
     - The original code would have freed the MR structure regardless of the success or failure of the deregistration, which could lead to a crash if the deregistration was retried.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a critical bug where the driver was incorrectly freeing the MR structure even when the deregistration failed. This could lead to a NULL pointer dereference if the deregistration was attempted again after the structure had already been freed.
- By adding the error check and preventing the free operation when an error occurs, the patch ensures that the MR structure remains valid for any subsequent operations, thus preventing system crashes related to dereferencing a freed pointer.
- The fix is directly related to the previous commit identified by the `Fixes` tag, which introduced the support for MRs with Huge pages, indicating that the issue arose from changes made in that commit.

Do not free the MR structures, when driver returns error to the stack.

Fixes: 872f3578241d ("RDMA/bnxt_re: Add support for MRs with Huge pages")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1574671174-5064-2-git-send-email-selvin.xavier@broadcom.com

Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the driver frees the memory region (MR) structure even when the deregistration of the MR fails, leading to a situation where the structure is accessed again after being freed, resulting in a NULL pointer dereference and a system crash. This improper handling of the MR structure during error conditions creates instability in the driver.

Here is the patch:
 
 int bnxt_re_dereg_mr(struct ib_mr *ib_mr, struct ib_udata *udata)
 {
 	struct bnxt_re_mr *mr = container_of(ib_mr, struct bnxt_re_mr, ib_mr);
 	struct bnxt_re_dev *rdev = mr->rdev;
 	int rc;
 
 	rc = bnxt_qplib_free_mrw(&rdev->qplib_res, &mr->qplib_mr);
-	if (rc)
+	if (rc) {
 		dev_err(rdev_to_dev(rdev), "Dereg MR failed: %#x\n", rc);
+		return rc;
+	}
 
 	if (mr->pages) {
 		rc = bnxt_qplib_free_fast_reg_page_list(&rdev->qplib_res,
 							&mr->qplib_frpl);
 		kfree(mr->pages);
 		mr->npages = 0;
 		mr->pages = NULL;
 	}
 	ib_umem_release(mr->ib_umem);
 
 	kfree(mr);
 	atomic_dec(&rdev->mr_count);
 	return rc;
 }
